issue_context.title: ADSP: Many kernel test cases which have CONFIG_MP_NUM_CPUS=1 failed in daily testing
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
About one half of test cases failed. The symptom is it hangs up without any log output. 
It only happens on test cases which CONFIG_MP_NUM_CPUS=1

 - What target platform are you using?  intel_adsp_cavs15
 - What have you tried to diagnose or workaround this issue? The PR https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/41283 will fix this problem. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
This is one example of running tests/kernel/mutex/mutex_api, any test case which has CONFIG_MP_NUM_CPUS=1 could reproduce it.
1. source zephry-env.sh
2. twister -p intel_adsp_cavs15 --device-testing -T tests/kernel/mutex/mutex_api --west-flash="/home/ztest/work/zephyrproject/zephyr/boards/xtensa/intel_adsp_cavs15/tools/flash.sh,/home/ztest/work/zephyrproject/modules/audio/sof/keys/otc_private_key.pem,/home/ztest/work/rimage/config,/home/ztest/work/rimage/build/rimage" --device-serial-pty="/home/ztest/work/zephyrproject/zephyr/boards/xtensa/intel_adsp_cavs15/tools/adsplog.py,--no-history" -vv


**Expected behavior**
The test case pass and show up its test result.

**Impact**
Many test cases failed, the pass rate drop about half.

**Logs and console output**
```
===
=== [Invalid slot 0; ADSP Device Reset?]
===
```
Then it will hang up until timeout, test cases failed.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Toolchain e.g Zephyr SDK 0.13.4
 - Commit SHA or Version used:

review_comments: Why take the address of these here when most/all of the uses below then deref it?

Clarity and style.  A macro being used like a pointer feels naturally like a MMIO register to me.  A macro that looks like data (and isn't otherwise used like memory, e.g. as a struct with fields as CAVS_SHIM is) seems weirder.  Non-pointer lvalues might be external memory, they might be local variables, nothing at the point where they're used tells you what they mean.
I suppose a smart compiler would remove the *(&(x)) and replace with x as well potentially, so I think that makes sense, do you know if gcc or xcc do that today? Mostly curious at this point.
I'm sure this is fine, but it stood out to me in reading this. Can you comment on why this is being removed?
c.f. huge essay in the commit message :)
Of course! I feel like github review doesn't always point me at the commit messages and log, I should look at those more on review. Will look, thanks!
